text.text: It's not the best, but it's not the WORST. Although I was only here for one night so I can't say. But the reviews are.. there. Only book this motel if you're on a budget and/or absolutely need somewhere to stay the night. The walls are super thin, and you can hear everything. So if you're a light sleeper, good luckkk. The bathroom is kinda gross (at least in the room I was in; trying to be nice). But not like, "I can't use the bathroom" gross, you can just visibly see some stains. Also, my sink was clogged? Ummmmm... whatever I guess. The bed is comfortable, but the sheets are... questionable... I found some hair that wasn't mine. The hallways STINK. Not sure if it's the staff who don't clean or the people who...? But anyways, so far, two staff that I've encountered during my visit were nice. So there's that. I had a bed, I was able to shower, I was able to sleep (a bit); that's all that mattered to me. THANKFULLY, no one tried getting into my room? I saw a review saying that someone tried getting into theirs I was like, oh shit. But overall, I don't think I'd consider this my go-to. But if I ABSOLUTELY needed to, it's an option.

text.text: I really don’t like the first floor, but the receptionist are really sweet people, love Mrs rose and Mrs Amy, even the two young men are nice, always tells me good morning and ask how is my day. The only thing I don’t care for is the smell in the hallways, because of the guests pets, it’s not the hotels fault, it’s the guest who lets their pets urinate and poop on the hallways floor. I also wish they had breakfast to go instead of only coffee, that would be great. I also like the location, which is very close to universal studios. Rooms are super clean and smells really nice, hallways again needs a lot of work, that’s why I only gave 4 stars

text.text: I was assigned to this hotel by Hotwire.  It is listed as a 2.5 star hotel, but it really is a one star hotel - similar to a half-way house.  It has long-term tenants, and it smelled really bad.  The carpets were really dirty, paint peeling off of the doors, broken door locks on exterior doors, the elevator was broken and there was a shopping cart at the front entrance.  Our neighbors tried to get into our room through the adjoining door and there was a domestic dispute in the hall-way.  When we checked out a half hour after check-in, the front desk acted like this was not out of the ordinary which is also concerning.  On top of all of this, they won't refund my room rate because they said "I used the room" by going into the room.  Horrible customer service, horrible hotel and they prey on out-of-towners as their business model.

text.text: I’m happy that I went to Motel 6, this was the lowlight of my trip. I get to tell my friends and family for the rest of my life about the cockroaches in my room, the bathroom not locking or closing, and the people screaming “get out of my hotel room”. Thank you motel 6, I will be back.

llm_analysis.top_distress_signals: Moderate-to-low rating with high review volume, increasing complaints related to cleanliness and maintenance issues such as dirtiness, odors, broken facilities, and pest problems, declining guest sentiment, and increasing negative review activity.
llm_analysis.investment_thesis: The property shows strong signs of operational distress driven by cleanliness and maintenance issues, reflected in declining guest sentiment and increased complaints despite stable branding and no immediate renovation needs. Ownership tenure is moderate, suggesting potential seller fatigue. The asset presents a solid opportunity for operational turnaround and repositioning to restore guest satisfaction and improve financial performance.
llm_analysis.review_summary: Guests frequently report issues with cleanliness, including dirt and pest problems, as well as maintenance concerns like broken fixtures and unpleasant odors. Complaints have increased recently despite a rise in review volume, indicating operational challenges. While the property does not currently require renovation, guest sentiment is declining, reflecting growing dissatisfaction with service and facility conditions.
